claims.text: Introducing dopants or defects into zirconia can modify its potential energy landscape.
Density functional theory can be used to identify or optimize dopants or defects that alter zirconia's potential energy landscape.
Modifying zirconia's potential energy landscape reduces the energy required for sintering.
The proposed dopant- or defect-mediated modification can reduce zirconia's sintering temperature by at least 100°C.
The proposed zirconia sintering process operates within a temperature range of 700–900°C.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction depends on the type and amount of dopants or defects.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction depends on the sintering conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention entails physically introducing dopants or defects selected using density functional theory, whereas the experiment compares samples with and without the 'application of density functional theory.' Density functional theory is a computational method rather than a physical sample treatment, so the experimental groups do not operationalize the stated intervention.
